rows.sourceText: 46 3.1.2 Nasal vowels It is extremely difficult to come up with nasal and non-nasal pairs of words to show contrast. However, we find all six nasal vowels. This can thus be regarded as a marginal suprasegmental feature of a small set of lexemes.  The fact that nasalization is not very robust in Darai is also referred to by Kotapish and Kotapish (1975:47). They note, "Nasalization occurs in Darai but varies from speaker to speaker."  The central nasal vowel /ã/ occurs more frequently than other nasal vowels. All the words containing the nasal vowels which occur in our discourse and elicited database are listed in (6). 2   (6) /bʰãtʰi/ ‘bellow’ /bãsi/  ‘flute’ /pãcəwə/ ‘fifth’  /ãṭo/  ‘seedling of barley or maize etc’  /cĩcbisə/ ‘a kind of louse’  /ciũṭa/  ‘seedling of barley or maize etc’  /dzʰə̃krija/ ‘a pot used to dry the meat’  /bʰəjẽ/  ‘floor’ /ɡahẽ/  ‘very much’ /kʰõkʰri/ ‘a by product in processing paddy into rice’ /ɡʰõuka/ ‘a kind of bucket where the fish are kept after they are caught’ /ãkʰi/  ‘eye’ /cʰõṭo/  ‘short’ /hõco/  ‘short’ /kə̃uri/  ‘soft’  3.1. 3 Diphthongs and vowel sequences Masica (1991:116) points out that the distinction between diphthongs and vowel sequences is complex in IA languages as vowel sequences often lead to diphthongs.
